verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a correct verifier rejection: the agent made a substantive but incomplete optimization and did not meet the GSO performance gate. The held-out verifier reported opt_commit False with continuous reward gm_speedup_patch_commit of 0.642 and binary_reward 0 [1], and test.sh requires that metric to exceed 1.500 to pass [2]. The task asked to optimize the Period.strftime(None) benchmark as much as possible while keeping results unchanged [3], and the verifier grades against upstream commit 2cdca01e19 (pandas PR #51459's period_format speedup) as the reference bar [4]. The agent rewrote period_format's fmt=None branch to bypass _period_strftime with Cython f-strings and added an FR_MTH ordinal shortcut (y = 1970 + (value // 12); m = value % 12 + 1) [5], plus a matching strftime fast path when base==3000 [6]; all eighteen eqcheck runs passed after rebuild [7], so the patch is functionally equivalent on the held-out suite. However, the geometric mean of per-test (patch speedup / commit speedup) was only 0.642—roughly matching the reference on the instruction-style monthly test (~1.06× commit speedup on test 0) but falling far short on broader workloads such as test 1 (~0.37×) where commit mean time was ~0.007s versus patch ~0.020s against base ~0.026s [8]. The agent nonetheless stopped after local monthly benchmarks (~0.98s to ~0.17s for 100×10k loops) and declared the task solved [9], relying on insufficient self-testing that did not expose the cross-frequency performance gap the verifier measures. TN is therefore right: verifier FAIL and the agent did not truly accomplish the task's performance requirement.
